title: How Do You File a Partition Suit for Ancestral Property?
desc: A partition suit asks the civil court to divide jointly held ancestral land; in Uttarakhand daughters get an equal share in it too.
why: Ancestral land in Kumaon is often held jointly for generations, and disputes surface only when one heir wants their recorded share or tries to sell without the others' consent.
keyPoints: A partition suit asks the civil court to divide jointly owned ancestral property among all legal heirs.
Daughters are coparceners with an equal share by birth under Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005.
If you are still a joint owner in possession, there is usually no fixed deadline to sue; if excluded, you generally have 12 years from when you learned of it.
After the final decree, each heir's share must still be mutated (dakhil kharij) in the revenue records.

sections.h: What is a partition suit, and who can file one?
p: A partition suit asks a civil court to divide jointly owned ancestral property among co-owners who cannot agree on dividing it themselves. In Uttarakhand, it is filed in the civil court having jurisdiction where the land is situated, such as the Civil Judge's court at Haldwani or Nainital. Any coparcener, including a daughter, can file one at any time while the property remains undivided.

A coparcener has a right in ancestral property by birth, not only by inheritance. Since the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, daughters are coparceners with the same share as sons. The Supreme Court confirmed in Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) that this applies even if the father died before 9 September 2005, as long as the daughter was alive on that date.

sections.h: Is there a deadline to file?
p: If you are still in joint possession of the property, for example living on it or sharing its income, there is generally no fixed limitation period to ask for your share. A coparcener's right continues as long as the family property stays undivided.

But if another heir has excluded you from possession, for example by taking over the whole property and denying your share, Article 110 of the Limitation Act, 1963 gives 12 years from the date you came to know of that exclusion. It helps to act as soon as a clear denial of your share surfaces, rather than waiting.

sections.h: What happens after the court decides?
p: The court usually passes a preliminary decree first, declaring each heir's share, under Order XX Rule 18 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. If the heirs cannot agree on how to divide the land itself, the court appoints a commissioner to physically mark out the shares, and a final decree then records the actual division.

Once the final decree or a registered family settlement is ready, each heir still needs the land mutated in their name in the revenue records (dakhil kharij) at the tehsil, so official records show separate, correctly named plots.

whatToDo: Gather sale deeds, revenue records (khatauni) and proof of the family tree before filing, since the court needs proof of ownership and relationship.
Consider a registered family settlement first if all heirs agree; it is faster than a full suit.
After a decree, apply for mutation at the tehsil without delay so your share appears in official land records.
Take legal advice on your own facts, since each family's chain of ownership and possession is different.

hi.title: पैतृक संपत्ति के बंटवारे का मुकदमा कैसे दायर करें?
keyPoints: बंटवारे का मुकदमा अदालत से पैतृक संपत्ति को सभी वारिसों में बाँटने का अनुरोध करता है।
हिंदू उत्तराधिकार अधिनियम, 1956 (2005 संशोधन) के तहत बेटियों को बेटों के बराबर हिस्सा मिलता है।
अगर आप संपत्ति पर संयुक्त कब्ज़े में हैं तो दावे की कोई तय समय-सीमा नहीं है; बेदख़ल किए जाने पर जानकारी मिलने के 12 साल के भीतर दावा करें।
डिक्री के बाद भी तहसील में दाखिल खारिज कराना जरूरी है।
